stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under key AI/ML tags including 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking around a significant open-source LLM.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring support for MLX, DFlash, and image input.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is introducing new limitations on 'full disk access' for macOS.
This change is a direct response to security risks amplified by the rise of AI agents.
The update aims to ensure users must intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A tech CEO was arrested in the US for allegedly smuggling $300M worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent issues surrounding the export controls and illicit trade of advanced AI hardware.
The story signals continued regulatory and enforcement challenges in the global semiconductor supply chain.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a generative language model.
The model utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the mainstream LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30-billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, supporting continuous context gathering and tool use for multi-step tasks.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, as validated by the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality responses.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: An OpenAI safety employee, David Robinson, has resigned from his role.
Robinson previously authored the safety reports for OpenAI's major model releases.
He is now publicly raising concerns about the safety aspects of OpenAI's technology in The Atlantic.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to mitigate potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns over AI agents accessing sensitive user data, such as private messages.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the sufficiency of existing regulatory frameworks (like the FDA) to control this access.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck in real-time animation of 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically requires costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method that approximates complex neural decoding using linear combinations of blendshapes.
This approach aims to replace per-frame heavy neural decoding with a much faster, shallow coefficient predictor for real-time performance.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Features runtime-free verifiable rewards, suggesting a novel and rigorous method for assessing the correctness of generated cybersecurity tool invocations.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces RPG, a framework for autonomous self-improvement of embodied agents (robots).
The method allows for skill improvement without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
RPG leverages offline datasets to construct simulated practice tasks using execution feedback.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities.
The system maintains a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve past environmental observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the high computational cost of real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to simplify animation.
Replaces expensive per-frame neural decoding with a shallow coefficient predictor based on blendshapes.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess genuine structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a new diagnostic tool to probe the underlying reasoning capabilities of LLMs.
The findings aim to systematically diagnose current LLM limitations and inform future improvements via post-training techniques.

stories.title: OpenAI safety leader quits, warning AI company's culture is 'broken'
stories.author: jethronethro
bullet_points: A key safety leader at OpenAI has resigned.
The resignation comes with a warning about the company's internal culture being 'broken'.
This signals potential internal turmoil or ethical concerns within a leading AI developer.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free execution of decision-making logic.
The models can process text to provide probabilistic answers for yes/no questions, choices, or scores.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and expanded GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden the range of supported models.
It enhances Ollama's MLX engine specifically for Apple silicon hardware.

stories.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Capcom is actively exploring the integration of AI into game development processes.
A programmer presented on the future evolution of the RE Engine, hinting at advanced technological integration.
The announcement signals a growing industry trend toward collaborative human-AI game creation.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows developers to create custom 'Muse gadgets' using the AI.
Suggested use cases include displaying reminders on E Ink screens or using it on HDMI sticks.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly changing its content strategy, moving away from high-profile, prestige productions.
This shift is evidenced by the termination or winding down of multiyear production deals with established directors.
The move signals a potential strategic pivot in how Netflix approaches content acquisition and creation compared to rivals.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced a new agent platform named Dots.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, suggesting a focus on professional applications.
Dots demonstrates capabilities beyond typical AI assistants, such as ordering food, while maintaining a professional tone.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon has a $1 billion initiative aimed at addressing negative public sentiment regarding its data centers.
The company received mixed reactions, being praised for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, Amazon faced criticism for allegedly minimizing the environmental impact and pollution associated with its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a significant lawsuit regarding the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
Critics argue that the settlement does not fully compensate the workers involved.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduction of ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge, using researchers to annotate which past papers were crucial to their own work.
This addresses a key gap in current AI research: the ability to sense which buried prior ideas can inspire novel scientific breakthroughs.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces SILSA, a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation.
Addresses limitations of current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
Uses compact sliding-window slice latents to represent shapes while preserving topology, aiming to reduce generation cost.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models, which limits bidirectional reasoning.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better capture of inter-token statistical dependencies.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: DMAD (Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation) is a new method for fast visual generation.
It reframes distribution matching as a classification problem to learn log-density ratios directly.
The technique aims to improve upon previous methods that required auxiliary diffusion models and extra computational cost.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex molecular topologies, such as ring systems and recurring motifs, which standard formalisms struggle with.
The framework aims to overcome the computational demands and decoding difficulties associated with existing higher-order representations in chemistry.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core method, Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA), trains a Transformer to forecast the next continuous embedding in a sequence.
This approach leverages the sequential nature of image generation (noisy to clean) to train the predictive model.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in existing methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) where surface fragmentation and topological inconsistency are common.
The core innovation is a topology-aware representation designed to improve consistency and reduce generation costs for complex shapes.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO is a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
It addresses the memory bottleneck caused by optimizer state, which limits the size of LLMs that can be trained on current GPUs.
TACO offers an alternative to existing methods (like Muon) by using a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach, aiming to maintain performance comparable to AdamW.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs, which involves moving mass between distributions while incurring a cost for visited states.
A key finding is that the complex learning approach (using temporal-difference penalties) can be replaced by a mathematical simplification: a Feynman-Kac tilt.
This tilt transforms the cost-augmented bridge into a standard bridge against a modified (tilted) reference process, allowing for exact computation.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, aiming to maintain inter-token dependencies.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order Optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size determination.
Uses a trusted first-order optimizer for direction while employing zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Focuses on runtime-free, verifiable rewards, aiming to rigorously test the syntactic correctness of LLM-generated cybersecurity tool invocations.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduction of ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
The benchmark leverages expert human knowledge by having researchers annotate which past works influenced their current projects.
The project addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within massive research archives to drive new scientific breakthroughs.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete diffusion models for language generation.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding, which breaks statistical dependencies.
Continuous diffusion models overcome this by denoising a shared continuous state, maintaining inter-token dependencies.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of context management in long-horizon coding agents.
Introduces AutoCompact, a method that trains agents to intelligently decide when and how to compact past context.
Focuses on enabling agents to handle complex, repository-level software engineering tasks effectively.

stories.title: From Knowledge Access to Source Learning: Developing Source-Specific Competence
stories.author: Haohan Wang
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap in LLM agent development where repeated use of the same external knowledge source is treated as mere access rather than an opportunity for deeper learning.
The paper introduces the concept of 'source learning,' aiming to develop reusable competence specifically tied to external knowledge sources.
This work builds upon existing methods for source content access and agent memory, pushing the frontier toward progressive understanding of persistent data.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper proposes a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to rigorously test and validate tool-use claims in smaller LLMs.
The study demonstrates false positives using matched-architecture Spanish security models, highlighting the limitations of lenient evaluation metrics.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper investigates methods for enhancing frontier models beyond standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior for generalization while SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting.
The proposed 'Finetuning with Sampling' introduces a new approach to improve learning efficiency and capability acquisition in post-training.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test data agents on complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The research introduces 'Where-OPD,' a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a privileged, self-generated supervision signal.
It addresses a gap in current MLLM research, moving beyond simple use of privileged visual cues like image crops.

stories.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
stories.author: bastitx
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Kolibri,' described as a sovereign open-weight model.
The announcement is accompanied by a detailed technical report and a supporting blog post.
The focus on 'sovereign' models suggests a trend toward localized or controlled AI deployments.

stories.title: I got targeted: Trying to get your credentials via a git post-checkout hook
stories.author: frankwiles.com by frankwiles
bullet_points: The article discusses a security vulnerability related to Git post-checkout hooks.
The core threat involves attackers attempting to steal user credentials via these hooks.
This highlights a specific, practical security risk within developer workflows.

stories.title: Nudging with Questions: Why Telling Your AI What to Fix Triggers an Apology Death Spiral (And How to Advance Juniors)
stories.author: randalschwartz
bullet_points: The article discusses the negative impact of direct, prescriptive instructions ('barking code fixes') on AI agents.
It proposes that using Socratic questioning techniques leads to significantly higher success rates (95%+ first-pass success) when guiding AI.
The concept is framed through the lens of mentoring experience, applying decades of teaching wisdom to modern agentic coding practices.
